messages:
Ravi Nair: Quick sync — need agreement on signal ownership for the new reliability dashboard. Scope: timeouts, 5xx, OOM, degraded-mode/fallback counts. Runtime/infra/console all need to feed this. Who owns what?
Megan Li: +1. We should standardize metric names/tags first. Proposed tags: service, route, model, region, deployment_tier, customer_id (hashed). Keep cardinality controls on customer_id.
Zoe Park: runtime can emit low-level counters and labels. We'll add `fallback_type` and `degraded_reason` when fallback happens. Counters we can emit: `redwood_request_timeout_total`, `redwood_response_5xx_total`, `redwood_oom_events_total`, `redwood_fallback_count_total`.
Juan Torres: infra will be responsible for aggregation, rollups, and retention. Prefer us to emit stable metric names and not rely on adhoc labels. We will add pipeline transforms to compute per-route rates and 7/30d baselines.
Alice Chen: From Console/UX: we need per-route and per-customer breakdowns, and a small "why-degraded" panel that shows top degraded reasons. Also need an opt-in for customers to see their own metrics vs. totals. UI wants a 90/99 latency histogram too.
Kevin O'Neill: Oncall note — include an explicit `degraded_mode` boolean and `degraded_reason` tag values: {model_unavailable, capacity_throttle, kv_cache_miss, internal_error}. That helps runbooks. Also emit a `fail_open` vs `fail_closed` flag for fallbacks.
Megan Li: Agree on naming. Couple of examples we should standardize in docs and the SDK: code block below with PromQL & proto-ish emission example:
```
# PromQL examples
rate(redwood_response_5xx_total{service="runtime", route="/v1/gen"}[5m])
sum by (route, model) (rate(redwood_fallback_count_total[1m]))

# emission pseudo-proto for runtime
metric RedwoodEvent {
  string name = 1; // e.g. "redwood_fallback_count_total"
  map<string,string> labels = 2; // route, model, region, fallback_type, degraded_reason
  int64 value = 3;
}
```
Zoe Park: Runtime note — we emit at request completion (or failure). For OOMs we only have coarse signals from the process supervisor now; we'll add an explicit exit-code label when possible. OOMs may need a separate stream with lower cardinality.
Juan Torres: Cardinality guardrails: infra will drop labels beyond team thresholds (e.g., no freeform user messages). We'll keep customer_id hashed and sampled. Also suggest a rollout plan: start with service-level totals, then route-level, then per-customer after 2 weeks.
Alice Chen: UX timeline — we can ship a skeleton dashboard for the web console in 2 weeks if metrics exist. Can we get a minimal set: `timeouts`, `5xx`, `fallback_count`, `oom_events`, and `latency_p95`?
Ravi Nair: That minimal set sounds good. Action items: (1) Zoe to submit metric PR with names & labels by EOD tomorrow. (2) Juan to prepare aggregation pipelines and retention policy draft by Friday. (3) Megan to add alert runbook mappings for each metric. (4) Alice to mock console widgets by next Tue.
observability-bot: Created Grafana draft dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd1234/reliability-runtime-signals (skeleton panels for timeouts/5xx/oom/fallbacks/latency).
Kevin O'Neill: Quick ask — include an alert that fires when fallback_rate > 5% for 5m for any production route. Also ensure alerts include `recent_top_degraded_reasons` as a field in pager payload.
Megan Li: I'll add those alert rules and link to runbooks. For paging payload we can attach a small table of top reasons computed by infra.
Zoe Park: One more runtime detail — fallback counts should include `fallback_source` (kv_cache, model_fallback, timeout_proxy). Will add to PR.
Juan Torres: Noted. I'll ensure infra preserves `fallback_source` label for top-k reasons and strips any high-cardinality labels during aggregation.
Ravi Nair: Great. If nobody objects, I'll schedule a 30-min sync Thursday to review the PR + Grafana draft. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
